# One regular-singleton dual for penalized shape and affine-buffer stationarity

This note combines the two parameter types in ONE actual physical-response
certificate. It retains every normalization and penalty term. It proves an
exact affine-moment identity, a stronger constraint on the location of
active sources, and a convex logarithmic base reserve. No assertion that
that reserve pays the full mixed cap deficit is made.

The setting is explicitly REGULAR and SINGLETON. The general supporting-
cap and multiple-contact problem is not replaced by this linear calculation.
Dependencies are the audited root source
`candidate 108870e8f9aac2e9`,
the physical response source
`candidate a7b11eee1eaaf72e`,
and signed speed addition in
`candidate 2951c303a65db1e9`.

## 1. Setting and physically addable variations

Let N=d+1 and let the actual positive compatible family have masses V_z,
M=sum V_z, volume weights w_z=V_z/M, within-fiber covariance Sigma, and
positive affine ell with

    sum_z w_z log ell_z=0,       P=sum_z w_z ell_z>=1.

Use f=(ell E/M)^(1/N), the covariance norm Gamma, and the penalized maximum

    J=beta+epsilon^2(P-1),
    beta=Q/M.

Assume this is a genuine joint local minimum and its maximum buffered
marks have proper own traces. Assume the chosen fixed covering groups
are regular in the full hyperplane parameters. The same-quantile theorem
then gives singleton faces p_i, with unique old marks y_i. Write

    Gamma(u_ij)=1,  sum_j rho_ij=1,
    B_i=sum_j rho_ij/S_ij,
    theta_ij=(rho_ij/S_ij)/B_i,
    delta_i=epsilon f_i/B_i>0.

The cap masses are Q, and the same finite groups cover all old maximizing
bases; strict gaps at the other bases persist under the proved continuation.

Take any convex cone of ACTUAL bounded signed radial speed arrays whose
finite sums have actual compatible realizations. The signed complete-cut
class is one such class. Continuous weighted boundary responses add;
selected cap responses add here precisely because they are regular.
For a chosen body speed v, simultaneously vary the unnormalized affine
parameter by ell+t phi, where phi is ANY affine function of the base,
and rescale geometrically using the actual new fiber volumes. Positivity
of ell makes both signs of each fixed phi feasible for small t. This
combines the body and parameter choices in one actual competitor; it is
not a formal freedom to alter a nonaffine function at selected bases.

## 2. The complete joint improvement functional

Let inward speed be positive for erosion. Define

    D_z=integral_boundary(K_z) v_z,  D=sum_z D_z,
    L_ij=actual fixed regular-cap loss,
    C_i=integral_boundary(K_pi) L_i(X)^(-N) v_pi(X),
    L_i(X)=1+a_i.(X-y_i),
    J_i^cov=sum_z integral_boundary(K_z)
                   [sum_j rho_ij(u_ij.(X-g_z))^2] v_z(X).

Here g_z is the ordinary centroid and a_i is the source projective
normalizer. Set

    s(v)=sum_z D_z log ell_z/M,
    A_phi=sum_z w_z phi(z)/ell_z.

Geometric normalization gives the COMBINED derivative

    dot ell_z/ell_z=s(v)+phi(z)/ell_z-A_phi.             (1)

The arithmetic factor's derivative is

    dot P=P_shape(v)+sum_z w_z phi(z)-P A_phi,
    P_shape(v)=sum_z D_z[P(1+log ell_z)-ell_z]/M.        (2)

The exact regular-singleton covering response says that the normalized
penalized cover has derivative -R_i(v,phi)/M, where

 R_i(v,phi)=sum_j theta_ij L_ij-beta D
  +delta_i [ C_i/(N E_i)+J_i^cov/(2M)-(N+2)D/(2NM)
             -s(v)/N-phi(p_i)/(N ell_i)+A_phi/N ]
  -M epsilon^2 [P_shape(v)+sum_z w_z phi(z)-P A_phi].    (3)

Every term is evaluated on the SAME actual deformation. In particular,
the shape-induced logarithmic scaling is not omitted when the free
parameter phi is varied, and the penalty is not removed from a body test.

If one combined direction makes all R_i strictly positive, exact contact
and quantile continuation gives an actual strict decrease of J. At the
assumed minimum this is impossible.

## 3. One separator handles body and parameter directions together

The finite response vectors (R_i) form a convex cone for the specified
physically addable class and signed affine parameter directions. Separating
it from the open positive orthant yields ONE set

    eta_i>=0,   sum_i eta_i=1,
    sum_i eta_i R_i(v,phi)<=0                            (4)

for EVERY permitted combined variation. No topological closedness of the
response cone is needed. The parameter-only directions have both signs,
so their part in (4) vanishes exactly. Hence, for every affine phi,

 sum_i eta_i delta_i phi(p_i)/ell_i
       +NM epsilon^2 sum_z w_z phi(z)
  =[Delta+NM epsilon^2 P] sum_z w_z phi(z)/ell_z,

    Delta=sum_i eta_i delta_i>0.                       (5)

This is the penalized multiplier equation with the SAME eta that tests
all physical speeds. Choosing unrelated separators for body and parameter
subproblems would not prove this conclusion.

## 4. Exact cancellation into one centered convex base function

Put

    a=Delta/(NM)>0,       kappa=a+epsilon^2 P>0,
    B(z)=epsilon^2(ell_z-P)-kappa log ell_z.            (6)

Define the actual weighted cap selector

    W_z(X)=sum_(i,j) eta_i theta_ij kappa_ij(z,X),

where kappa_ij is the regular cap's inward boundary-loss selector. The
complete physical density in (4), after (5) has canceled the free phi
part, is

 Xi_z(X)=W_z(X)-beta
    +sum_i eta_i delta_i 1_(z=p_i) L_i(X)^(-N)/(N E_i)
    +(1/(2M))sum_(i,j) eta_i delta_i rho_ij
                                      (u_ij.(X-g_z))^2
    -(N+2)a/2+B(z).                                   (7)

The remaining certificate is exactly

    sum_z integral_boundary(K_z) Xi_z(X)v_z(X)<=0       (8)

for every allowed physical speed array. Deriving (7) is just collecting
the actual shape-normalization contribution -Delta s/N and the penalty
-M epsilon^2 P_shape; together they yield B(z). There is no residual
unwritten logarithmic term.

The new base function has the exact conservation and curvature identities

    sum_z w_z B(z)=0,
    Hess_base B=kappa (grad ell)(grad ell)^T/ell^2.     (9)

Thus it is a convex base function of zero V-weighted mean. Common fiber-
affine motions remain null: their masses change proportionally, so s=0,
P_shape=0, and the weighted sum of B contributes zero. The already proved
cap/energy/covariance cancellation handles the remaining terms.

Zero weighted mean does NOT make B pointwise nonnegative or nonpositive.
An actual normalization calibration is two equal-volume fibers on bases
0,1 with ell=(1/2,2). Then P=5/4 and geometric mean is one, while

    B(0)=-3epsilon^2/4+kappa log 2,
    B(1)= 3epsilon^2/4-kappa log 2=-B(0).

Since kappa>=5epsilon^2/4 and log 2>2/3, B(0)>0 and B(1)<0.
The logarithm bound follows by strict midpoint Jensen for integral_1^2 1/t.
This is an actual body/parameter calibration, not a claimed stationary
penalized minimum. It rules out an unconditional sign shortcut for (6).

## 5. The exact active-source location constraint

Let

    nu=sum_i [eta_i delta_i/(NM)] delta_(p_i),
    Z=sum_z w_z/ell_z,
    g_tilt=(sum_z w_z z/ell_z)/Z,
    g_vol=sum_z w_z z.

Equation (5) is the AFFINE-MOMENT identity

    nu/ell+epsilon^2 w  ==aff  kappa w/ell.            (10)

The equality symbol means identical mass and first base moment; it does
not identify the discrete measures pointwise. Testing constants shows

    |nu/ell|=kappa Z-epsilon^2>0.

Let h be the barycenter of nu/ell. It is a convex combination of actual
active witness bases. Then

    h=[kappa Z g_tilt-epsilon^2 g_vol]
                                /[kappa Z-epsilon^2]. (11)

Thus this EXTRAPOLATED tilted barycenter must belong to the convex hull
of the active witnesses. The penalty pushes h beyond g_tilt away from
g_vol; it cannot simply be ignored in that location condition.

There is a sharp additional scalar consequence when ell is nonconstant
on the sampled base. Strict weighted AM--GM and Jensen give P>1 and Z>1.
Affineness gives ell(g_vol)=P and ell(g_tilt)=1/Z. Substituting (11), and
using kappa=a+epsilon^2 P, yields

    ell(h)=a/(kappa Z-epsilon^2)<1/Z<1<P.              (12)

The first strict comparison is equivalent to epsilon^2(PZ-1)>0.
Therefore at least one positively weighted active source has ell(p_i)<1.
More precisely the inverse-ell active weighted mean is the left side
of (12), not merely an unspecified point in conv I. If ell is constant,
normalization forces ell=1 and (10)--(12) reduce to the ordinary volume
barycenter condition. These are necessary consequences of an interior
regular-singleton joint minimum, not a claim that such witnesses pay
all mass on other bases.

## 6. A strict Jensen reserve on actual anchored base relations

For any actual anchored relation z0=sum_j lambda_j z_j and positive affine
ell, formula (6) gives the exact identity

 sum_j lambda_j B(z_j)-B(z0)
   =kappa [log ell(z0)-sum_j lambda_j log ell(z_j)]>=0. (13)

The affine epsilon^2 ell contribution cancels exactly. Equality holds
precisely when all positively weighted ell(z_j) are equal. If ell<=Lmax
on the relation, strong convexity of -log on that interval gives the
explicit bound

 sum_j lambda_j B(z_j)-B(z0)
   >=kappa/(2Lmax^2) sum_j lambda_j
                                  (ell(z_j)-ell(z0))^2. (14)

This is a genuine positive reserve tied to actual integer-base barycentric
relations, with no projective transformation of the lattice. However,
(8) does not automatically supply a martingale, contact allocation, or
correctly signed transport which spends (13). No such object is inferred
from the affine-moment identity (10), which controls only two moments.
The full cap indicators, energy losses, and covariance terms in (7)
remain present. Turning this exact reserve into a global payment theorem
is a further geometric obligation.

## 7. A surface-weighted contact-transport restriction

For this section, take the full actual response cone containing every
finite continuous convex physical function Phi(z,X), with either sign of
its values, as the common inward speed on sampled boundaries. This is a
proved class: use the same signed convex field on every plane of a complete
global support array. Hence the SAME dual in (7) satisfies

    integral Xi Phi d sigma<=0                        (15)

for every such Phi, where sigma is the sum of the actual fiber SURFACE
measures, with the base labels retained. Affine functions and their
negatives are included. They force equal mass and first physical moment
for the two Jordan measures

    mu=Xi_+ d sigma,       nu=Xi_- d sigma.

The compact convex-order/martingale theorem proved in
`candidate 6eda5637cc09a539`
therefore gives a coupling pi from mu to nu whose conditional target mean
is the actual source (z,X). These are precisely the Jordan SURFACE
marginals of the NEW Xi; they are not original fiber-volume marginals and
are not the old cap-profile measure.

Write Xi=Xi0+B(z), where Xi0 is (7) without its final B. The function B
has a finite convex extension to all physical space. Indeed extend -log t
below min_P ell>0 by its tangent line there; this is globally finite convex,
and agrees with -log ell on the sampled base hull. The affine epsilon^2
term is unchanged.
Testing this extension in (15) proves the nontrivial coercive restriction

    integral B(z)^2 d sigma <= -integral Xi0 B(z) d sigma.       (16)

All surface weights in this formula are essential. In particular
sum V_z B(z)=0 does not cancel either side. For an actual illustration,
take two equal-area fibers, a unit square and a 2-by-1/2 rectangle, on a
binary base, and ell=(1/2,2). Their perimeters are 4 and 5, so the same
B values in Section 4 have surface sum 4B(0)+5B(1)=-B(0), although their
volume-weighted sum is zero.

The coupling gives more than the test alone. Since ell is affine in the
base and E[Z'|Z,X]=Z, its conditional mean is E[ell(Z')|Z,X]=ell(Z).
The affine term of B cancels conditionally, giving the EXACT identity

 -integral Xi0 B d sigma-integral B^2 d sigma
    =kappa integral [log ell(Z)-E(log ell(Z')|Z,X)] d mu
    >= kappa/(2ell_max^2) integral
                                  (ell(Z')-ell(Z))^2 d pi.      (17)

The last inequality is the strong convexity of -log on the compact positive
range of ell. Equality in the nonquantitative Jensen gap holds exactly
when ell(Z')=ell(Z) almost surely conditionally. Thus the old part Xi0
must fund both the square in (16) and all ell-changing transport.

This transport actually respects supporting contact geometry. At a
sigma-regular source (p,X), let u be its continuous outward normal and
choose a feasible global supporting plane ell_p(u,z), affine in z and
touching h_p(u). For clarity, its existence follows from the finite
canonical support LP: at fixed u, maximize sum_z lambda_z h_z(u) subject
to sum lambda_z z=p and sum lambda_z=1. Canonical compatibility makes its
value h_p(u); finite LP dual attainment supplies exactly the required
affine majorant, also at boundary bases. A constant majorant is feasible,
so the finite dual has no feasibility issue. All target points of the coupling lie in the canonical
body. The nonnegative affine slack

    ell_p(u,Z')-u.X'

has conditional expectation equal to its source value zero, by the actual
physical martingale mean. Hence it vanishes on conditional targets. Its
two nonnegative components ell_p(u,Z')-h_(Z')(u) and h_(Z')(u)-u.X' each
vanish. Targets are therefore on the SAME actual supporting contact plane
and their own u-faces. The finite base probabilities lambda_z obey

    sum_z lambda_z z=p,
    sum_z lambda_z h_z(u)=h_p(u).                       (18)

They are tight actual anchored support representations. At regular target
points their continuous normal also equals u; nonregular target sets have
zero nu mass. The vector conditional-mean identity holds on one full source-measure
set, and on that set the argument works for EVERY supporting plane at
the given source; no measurable plane selection is needed. Alternatively
the archived continuous complete support baselines give such a selection.
The plane always has the specified NONZERO continuous normal u; a pure-
base support plane alone would not prove (18). No external lattice
transformation or guessed contact distribution is being introduced.

Equations (16)--(18) are a rigorously testable contact restriction, beyond
separate parameter balance. They do not force B=0: Xi0 can compensate it,
and transport can stay within an ell level. The affine-moment identity
(10) alone does not supply this martingale; the FULL signed convex-potential
tests (15), with their explicitly identified Jordan marginals, are needed.

### Exact zero-reserve rigidity and a quantitative version

Let the nonnegative reserve in (17) be

    R=-integral Xi0 B d sigma-integral B^2 d sigma.

If R=0, every such martingale preserves ell exactly on its edges. Thus
there is NO transport funding between different sampled ell levels. Since
P is finite, the coupling decomposes into finitely many blocks indexed by
those levels. Each block separately has equal Jordan mass and first
physical moment and satisfies convex order. Equivalently, on each level
set of bases the signed boundary measure Xi d sigma has zero affine
moments and nonpositive integral against every finite convex physical test.

If ell is injective on the sampled bases, these statements hold separately
on EVERY fiber, even when that fiber is not independently movable. This
conclusion comes from the globally existing transport and its zero reserve,
not from deleting other-fiber terms in an arbitrary dual. In d=2 the
archived planar face decomposition then applies fiber by fiber: Xi vanishes
on the nonfacet boundary and has its one-dimensional convex order separately
on each actual facet. Injectivity and R=0 remain additional hypotheses.

More quantitatively, if distinct sampled ell levels have minimum spacing
gap>0, (17) implies

    pi{ell(Z')!=ell(Z)} <= 2ell_max^2 R/(kappa gap^2).  (19)

Thus the reserve controls all cross-level Jordan SURFACE transport. For
any union of complete level blocks, the difference of its two Jordan
masses is bounded by the right side of (19). This is a direct accounting
consequence of the coupling; it is not an original-volume mass bound.

Neither stationarity nor volume centering of B proves R=0. Equation (19)
is useful only with an additional upper bound on the actual old-part
correlation that defines R, and no such bound is asserted here.

## 8. Scope

The common certificate, centered base potential, and active-source
location formula are new exact joint consequences beyond separate shape
and parameter stationarity. Their proof uses the actual response cone
and the audited contact continuation, not a differentiability assertion
for the maximum itself. All regular-singleton premises are explicit.

At positive-area supports the response is nonlinear in its solved
threshold shifts; at multiple contacts the minimum must be retained.
Neither case is silently promoted to (3)--(8). The penalty's relative
size is never assumed negligible, and (13) is not claimed to settle OC.

The companion `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_joint_penalized_affine_buffer_dual_defect_transport.py`
passes 780 exact symbolic/rational checks. It independently assembles the
raw-mass and penalty derivative, checks the simultaneous normalization and
collected density, and verifies the active-barycenter and Jensen algebra.
Actual response realization, finite separation, and the contact-martingale
argument are the analytic proofs above, not conclusions from scalar tests.
